lines.text: This is Parseley: your clipboard, with the math already done.
Everything you copy is kept. Copy some numbers, open the panel, and the stats are already there.
Press Command 1 to copy the sum, ready to paste.
One click reshapes a list: into a sequel IN clause, JSON, a sorted list, and more.
Type a greater-than sign to run anything by name. Sum, then Return, pastes the total right where you were typing.
Need a running total across apps? Start a series. Every number you copy is added. Copies with text are skipped, and one click adds them back.
Control, Option, Command, V pastes the total. Not the numbers: the answer.
Filling in a form? Select a few clips, queue them, and paste them one by one with the same shortcut.
Modes adapt to the app you're in: Finance in Excel, sequel in your database tool.
Copied a spreadsheet range? Pick a column to see just its stats.
Copied some JSON? Press Command J to see it as a graph. Long lists show their first five, and you can expand the rest or copy any path.
In the terminal there's a parseley command, and an M C P server, so Claude can use it too.
And everything stays on your Mac. No network. No accounts.
That's Parseley. Change any shortcut in Settings, and happy copying.
